paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to hold onto. Somebody was spreading the word that the Day of the Lord had already come, and Paul told the Thessalonians not to be easily disconcerted or alarmed (2 Thessalonians 2:2). Panic is loud, and it loves to dress up like it came from a trusted source. So when a message shows up shouting that everything is falling apart, check it against what God has already said.

Paul doesn't hide that hard things are coming. The lawless one will arrive with "every kind of power, sign, and false wonder," and his deceptions land on those who refused "the love of the truth" (2 Thessalonians 2:9-10). Notice that the problem isn't that the signs were too impressive, it's that people turned away from loving the truth. And Paul says the Lord Jesus will slay the lawless one with the breath of His mouth (2 Thessalonians 2:8), so I don't need to be nervous about how this ends.

Then Paul turns and says, "But we should always thank God for you, brothers who are loved by the Lord…" (2 Thessalonians 2:13). God chose them from the beginning and called them through the gospel, so that they may share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ (2 Thessalonians 2:13-14). So what do we do while we wait? "Stand firm and cling to the traditions we taught you" (2 Thessalonians 2:15). And you don't do it alone, baker, because Jesus and the Father have given us eternal comfort and good hope, and They strengthen you in every good word and deed (2 Thessalonians 2:16-17).
